project.name: relay
project.identity: A private, keyboard-first macOS control plane for personal AI coding workflows with Today, Playbook, and Usage surfaces.
project.audience: The owner coordinating recurring local AI coding workflows who needs fast capture, explicit playbooks, and visible usage state.
project.core_loop: Capture a work item or workflow, route it through the appropriate playbook, inspect usage and release evidence, and keep execution or external effects behind explicit gates.
project.north_star: The owner can move recurring AI coding work through a fast local control surface without losing context, usage visibility, or release ownership.
not_this: A hidden capture or submission agent
A release authority that bypasses separate capture and release gates

mvp.definition: The owner can use the local Today and Playbook surfaces to capture and route a recurring AI coding task with visible usage and explicit next action.

complete_product.definition: Relay provides a reliable private control plane for recurring AI coding work with durable playbooks, usage evidence, recoverable capture, and separate release gates.

outcomes.name: A recurring coding task can move quickly from capture into the correct playbook with enough context to continue safely.

layers.intended: The owner spends less effort navigating workflow state and more effort on the work itself.
layers.planned: The project defines Today, Playbook, and Usage surfaces for personal AI coding workflows.
layers.implemented: The repository contains the private local control-plane implementation.
layers.verified: README and AGENTS establish the scope; live keyboard, capture, and accessibility behavior was not run here.

evidence.note: Defines Relay's private keyboard-first control-plane scope and surfaces.

blockers.summary: Live capture, keyboard, accessibility, and workflow continuation evidence remain unverified.

outcomes.name: Usage and release state are visible while capture and release remain separate, explicit, and owner-controlled.

layers.intended: A private control surface should not blur local workflow state with release or external effects.
layers.planned: The project separates capture and release gates and includes Usage as a first-class surface.
layers.implemented: The repository documents and implements the corresponding local surfaces.
layers.verified: No release or usage-gate execution was performed in this bootstrap.

evidence.note: Documents Today, Playbook, Usage, and separate capture/release gates.

blockers.summary: The live gate sequence and owner-controlled recovery path still require execution evidence.

intended.note: Private product identity and workflow loop.

planned.note: Today, Playbook, Usage, and gate scope.

verified.note: Repository operating constraints; no live UI or gate execution here.

drift.summary: Relay is treated as an experimental private tool: its intended keyboard-first workflow and separate gates are documented, but live capture, usage, accessibility, and release evidence are not established.

evidence.note: Documents the experimental local workflow surface.
